author: whlym
assistance: AI-assisted development, review and release preparation
scope: Original project scripts adapted for public release. Original private filesystem locations and research inputs are intentionally not included.

changes: Renamed optional school_package_manifest.json to generic package_manifest.json; existing records remain schema v2.
Preserved protocol settings, identity hashes, pilot-review gate, run locks, segment prefix rules and dual checkpoint slots.
No school job submission or queue adapter is included.
Replaced hard-coded target residue highlights with repeatable --highlight-residue.
Removed school-specific wording from a legacy engineering warning.
Added zero-candidate N/O hydrogen-bond handling: shape-preserving empty arrays, no empty geometry calls, empty occupancy tables and zero occupied-pair count; covered by synthetic test.
Scientific distance/angle criteria and valid-manifest handling retained.
No semantic changes; text line endings may be normalized by Git.

files.source_label: New generic public assembler adapted from internal existing-evidence demo main.py
changes: Replaced fixed three-molecule/two-target research schema with declared candidates and targets.
Added explicit schema validation, duplicate/missing-pair rejection, path confinement, finite-number checks, SHA verification and output-preservation guard.
Added explicit unavailable/provisional/completed-reviewed MD status; no automatic candidate selection.
Replaced real research inputs with hand-written synthetic fixtures; numerical values are invented and marked.

tests: Public tests are new self-contained standard-library and optional synthetic-geometry fixtures. They neither run MD nor redistribute old trajectories.
dependencies: Dependency code, molecular preparation parameters and model weights are not vendored; see root requirements files and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
compatibility: Renamed package/task manifests are a public packaging change. Copying public scripts into an existing frozen research deployment is not a supported migration; retain its original runner and environment for resume.
